classification.difficultyReason: A modelling task: speed and time give arc length, then the angle, then height as 22 − 20cos θ measured from the lowest point. Needs a context-to-trig representation change with no angle shown and a radians calculator evaluation, but it is a single path.

content.prompt: A Ferris wheel of radius $20\text{ m}$ has its lowest point $2\text{ m}$ above the ground. A passenger boards at the lowest point and is carried around at a steady $0.5\text{ m/s}$. How high above the ground is the passenger after $80$ seconds, correct to the nearest $0.01$ metre?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}l&=vt\\l&=0.5\times80\\l&=40\text{ m}\\l&=r\theta\\40&=20\theta\\\theta&=2\text{ radians}\end{align*}$$
The centre is $2+20=22\text{ m}$ above the ground. The passenger is $\theta$ from the lowest point, so is $20\cos\theta$ below the centre. Using radian mode:
$$\begin{align*}h&=22-20\cos2\\h&\approx30.32\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
